title: Lift an annihilated abelian sheaf to constant-ring-valued module sheaves
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $n\geq0$, and $G$ an abelian sheaf on its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. If $n\operatorname{id}_G=0$, then there exists a sheaf $M$ valued in $\operatorname{Mod}(\operatorname{ULift}(\mathbf Z/n))$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] whose underlying abelian sheaf is isomorphic to $G$.

source.place: First step of the parent proof: sectionwise module structure; construction implicit in Tag 03RW

proof.text: Evaluate the annihilation equation at every object and section. Use Mathlib AddCommGroup.zmodModule to equip each section group with its Z/n-module structure and ULift.module for lifted scalars. Additive restriction maps are linear by ZMod.map_smul. Functor laws follow from those of the original sheaf. This is valid also at n=0, n=1 and for the zero sheaf.

The underlying abelian presheaf is definitionally the original presheaf. ModuleCat forgetting to abelian groups reflects limits, so Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp proves the module presheaf is a sheaf. Iso.refl gives the claimed underlying-sheaf isomorphism.

blueprint_update.statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $n\geq0$, and $G$ an abelian sheaf on its small etale site. If $n\operatorname{id}_G=0$, then there exists a sheaf $M$ of $\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$-modules on the small etale site of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] whose underlying abelian sheaf is isomorphic to $G$.

proof.text: Evaluating $n\operatorname{id}_G=0$ at every object $U$ shows that $n$ kills every section group $G(U)$. An abelian group killed by $n$ is uniquely a $\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$-module, with $(k\bmod n)\cdot a=ka$. Every additive map between such groups is $\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$-linear, so the restriction maps of $G$ are linear, and the functor laws follow from those of $G$. This defines a presheaf $M$ of $\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$-modules; the argument is valid also for $n=0$, $n=1$ and for the zero sheaf.

The underlying abelian presheaf of $M$ is $G$ itself. The forgetful functor from $\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$-modules to abelian groups preserves and reflects limits, so $M$ satisfies the sheaf condition because $G$ does. The identity gives the claimed isomorphism of underlying abelian sheaves. ([def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]).
